subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value:
A TWO-WEB REGISTER TRANSPOSITION CAN BE COMPLETELY INVISIBLE IN THE RAW BYTE DIFF AT THE EXACT PLACE THAT EXPLAINS IT - ITS OWN DEFINITIONS - BECAUSE REORDER AND RENAME CANCEL THERE. When they do, verify_consistent_recolor refuses the recolor, and the refusal it prints points at a USE far away from the real cause. Modelling the definition pair as a permutation window is what makes the transposition provable, and it converts an `unproven_recolor_audit` escape into a fully machine-proven rule. MEASURED on game/anim/atree::fn_8001267C, 2026-09-01, closing it byte-exact.

THE SHAPE. Our build colours a loop's two induction webs r4 and r3; the target colours the SAME two webs r3 and r4 - a clean 2-cycle. Inside the loop every use differs and reads as ordinary recolor material (ours `addi r3,r3,1` / `add r5,r0,r4` / `addi r4,r4,0x24` / `cmpw r3,r0` against the target's `addi r4,r4,1` / `add r5,r0,r3` / `addi r3,r3,0x24` / `cmpw r4,r0`). But the two DEFINITIONS, `li r4,0` at +0x178 and `li r3,0` at +0x17c, are BYTE-IDENTICAL between the two objects. They are identical precisely BECAUSE the transposition is exact and the two streams emit the pair in opposite order: applying the swap and then the renaming returns the same two words. So the one place in the function that would explain the whole recolor contributes ZERO differing words, and any diff-driven or positional analysis walks straight past it.

WHY THE CHECKER THEN REFUSES, AND WHY THE MESSAGE MISLEADS. verify_consistent_recolor infers the renaming FORWARD from each definition's own register fields via _map_define. At two identical defs it therefore records the IDENTITY map g3->3, g4->4 - which is one of two equally byte-consistent readings, and the wrong one. It then refuses at the first swapped USE it reaches, here `+0x1c8: use of g3 does not correspond to g4 under the running renaming`. +0x1c8 is a `cmpw` 0x50 bytes past the actual cause and is not defective in any way. DO NOT diagnose from the offset the refusal names: walk BACK to the last definition of the named register and check whether its defining word is identical in both streams. If it is, suspect this law.

THE FIX, AND IT IS A RULE-AUTHORING FIX, NOT A CHECKER FIX. Add a permutation window over the definition pair - here [0x178,0x180) order [1,0]. The permutation is legal on its face (two independent constant loads to distinct registers; check_permutation_dependences ACCEPTS with exit_dead=None) and it is not a trick: the two webs really are defined in opposite order in the two streams, and the byte identity is the artifact, not the reorder. After it, copy_register_fields sees our `li r3,0` where the target has `li r4,0` and records g3->4, and vice versa, so the running renaming enters the loop already carrying the transposition and every downstream use verifies. On fn_8001267C this took the rule from `unproven_recolor_audit` (whole-function recolor unproven, warning printed) to fully proven, with the audit key deleted.

THREE COROLLARIES WORTH THE LINE. (1) A window whose before/after bytes are IDENTICAL to the target is still a legitimate and sometimes necessary permutation window; do not filter candidate windows by 'has differing words', which is what every current census does. (2) The ambiguity exists only because both registers hold the SAME VALUE at the defs - here both are `li ...,0`. Two defs of DIFFERENT constants would pin the pairing and this law would not fire. That is also the shape of the narrow sound checker extension, if anyone wants one: at a definition whose two candidate registers provably hold the same constant, both pairings are admissible and the checker could defer instead of committing to identity. Until that exists, the permutation window is the supported route. (3) attempt.CN_camera-mode-level-cluster-a-readiness.20260901.v1 concludes that camera_mode_level's remainder 'is not a bijective renaming either' from a refusal of exactly this shape (`+0x8b8: use of g27 does not correspond to g29 under the running renaming'). That conclusion was reached the same way and should be RE-DERIVED against this law before it is relied on - a coalescing diagnosis drawn from a forward-inference refusal is not safe evidence on its own. This law does not by itself close camera_mode_level (its +0x8b0 site is an independent form-plus-recolor blocker), but it does undermine one of the three reasons that function is believed unreachable.
